items.abstract: In autonomous driving systems, enabling vehicles to comprehend and execute high-level semantic instructions from humans is a crucial direction for advancing natural interactive navigation. To this end, this paper proposes a vision-language model guided semantic-aware diffusion navigation method (VLSAN) for semi-structured campus road scenarios, establishing a strategy for translating natural language instructions into vehicle motion control. The method takes natural language, raw images, and their high-dimensional visual features as joint inputs, leveraging the vision-language model (VLM) to generate semantically guided drivable semantic region maps, achieving multimodal information fusion and semantic alignment.

items.title: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
items.topic: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
items.summary: Cyclist fatality rates remain high despite policy support for active travel, and autonomous vehicles add complexity to mixed traffic. Neither crash statistics nor multi-model detection pipelines scale to continuous monitoring of perceived safety along a route. We present an edge-assisted crowdsensing system: handlebar cameras supply street-level frames, a vision-language model (VLM) turns each frame into structured traffic attributes through a single prompt, and an explainable boosting machine (EBM) combines them with OpenStreetMap road infrastructure and on-bike kinematics to predict a crowdsourced 1-9 safety score.

items.title: Competent Autonomous Driving Through Fine Tuning Vision Language Action Models with Symbolic Traffic Rules
items.topic: Competent Autonomous Driving Through Fine Tuning Vision Language Action Models with Symbolic Traffic Rules
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a unified approach to perception, reasoning, and control for autonomous driving, but accurate action prediction alone does not establish compliance with traffic regulations. This paper presents a rule-guided VLA framework that incorporates symbolic traffic-rule feedback into policy optimisation. The framework combines supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations with reinforcement learning (RL) refinement using a reward that encourages encoded-rule compliance while penalising deviations from expert actions.
